# Story 21 — Portal identity: registration, sign-in, password reset and the portal shell (Story: 512)

## Prerequisites

- **Story 2.1 completed** — the second Sanctum guard, `portal_accounts` table, and `PortalAccount` model already exist. Verify: `backend/config/auth.php` (guards `portal` at ~line 60, provider `portal_accounts` at ~line 94, passwords broker `portal_accounts` at ~line 132–134), `backend/app/Modules/Portal/Domain/PortalAccount.php`, `backend/app/Modules/Portal/Database/Migrations/2026_09_01_000100_create_portal_accounts_table.php`, and `backend/tests/Feature/Security/GuardIsolationTest.php`.
- **Story 1.3 completed** — the Next.js shell, design system, locale layer, and formatting layer are in place (`frontend/app/layout.tsx`, `frontend/components/shell/`, `frontend/components/i18n/IntlProvider.tsx`, `frontend/lib/i18n/`).
- **Customers module in place** — `backend/app/Modules/Customers/Domain/Customer.php`, `ContactIdentifier.php`, `IdentifierNormaliser.php`, and `DuplicateDetector.php` are available for the "link by email or create" flow.
- **Precedent** — Staff auth pattern in `backend/app/Modules/Security/Http/Controllers/AuthController.php`, `PasswordResetController.php`, and `ProfileController.php`; frontend precedent in `frontend/app/(auth)/` and `frontend/components/screens/auth/SignInForm.tsx`.

---

## Story Goal

Give a customer a first-class portal identity separate from staff:

1. Register a portal account with name, email, password, and preferred locale; on registration, link to an existing `customers` row by normalised email or create one.
2. Sign in / sign out over the `portal` Sanctum SPA cookie guard.
3. Request a password-reset link by email and complete reset via a time-limited, single-use token from the `portal_accounts` passwords broker.
4. Serve the portal at a **separate Next.js route group** `(portal)` with its own shell — slim top bar, mobile-first, no sidebar, three destinations: **My requests**, **New request**, **Account** — sharing the design system, locale, and formatting layers only.
5. Guarantee that a portal account cannot access any staff surface — neither via `/api/v1/*` staff endpoints nor via staff routes in the Next app.
6. Rate-limit registration, sign-in and password-reset endpoints.
7. Bilingual EN/AR with genuine RTL, and consistently use the word **request** (never "ticket") in customer-facing copy.

**Out of scope (visible in mockup but not this story):** brand swap (logo, primary colour, header), Help centre destination, CSAT prompt, anonymous-request claim flow, request creation/list itself (Story 6.2), any staff capability wiring on portal accounts.

## Product rules (from story)

- **Two guards, two tables, no discriminator column.** A portal account is never a staff user.
- Portal shell has **no sidebar** and a **slim top bar**; three destinations: **My requests**, **New request**, **Account**.
- Copy uses **request** — audit new portal strings; do **not** introduce "ticket".
- No branding customisation (no logo upload, no primary-colour override, no header configuration).
- **Rate-limit** registration, sign-in, and password-reset (both forgot and reset) endpoints.

### 2 — Portal controllers (Sanctum cookie mode, `portal` guard)

Create file: `backend/app/Modules/Portal/Http/Controllers/PortalAuthController.php`
- `register(RegisterPortalAccountRequest $req)`:
  1. Look up an existing `Customer` by normalised email through `IdentifierNormaliser` + `ContactIdentifier` join (kind = `ContactKind::Email`). If none, create a `Customer` in the default state from `CustomerState` and add the contact identifier.
  2. Create the `PortalAccount` with hashed password (`Hash::make`), assign FK `customer_id`, set `preferred_locale`.
  3. Log the actor in on the `portal` guard: `Auth::guard('portal')->login($account, $remember=false)`.
  4. Regenerate session: `$req->session()->regenerate()`.
  5. Return a portal user shape (see task 3).
- `login(PortalLoginRequest $req)`:
  - `Auth::guard('portal')->attempt(...)` on the normalised email. Regenerate session on success. On failure, throw a Problem 401 via the existing `ProblemDetails` pipeline (`backend/app/Modules/Platform/Http/ProblemDetails.php`).
  - Emit an event analogous to `StaffAuthAttempted` (see below).
- `logout(Request $req)`:
  - `Auth::guard('portal')->logout()`, invalidate session, regenerate CSRF token; mirror `AuthController::logout`.
- `me(Request $req)`:
  - Return the current portal-user shape.

- `reset(PortalResetPasswordRequest $req)` — `Password::broker('portal_accounts')->reset(...)`; on success `Hash::make` the new password and persist `remember_token = Str::random(60)`.

### 7 — Route registration and rate limits

File: `backend/routes/api.php`
- After the existing staff auth block (currently ~lines 54–70), append a new **portal** group:

```php
Route::prefix('portal')->name('portal.')->group(function (): void {
    Route::post('/auth/register', [PortalAuthController::class, 'register'])
        ->middleware('throttle:portal-register')
        ->name('auth.register');
    Route::post('/auth/login', [PortalAuthController::class, 'login'])
        ->middleware('throttle:portal-login')
        ->name('auth.login');
    Route::post('/auth/password/forgot', [PortalPasswordResetController::class, 'sendResetLink'])
        ->middleware('throttle:portal-password')
        ->name('auth.password.forgot');
    Route::post('/auth/password/reset', [PortalPasswordResetController::class, 'reset'])
        ->middleware('throttle:portal-password')
        ->name('auth.password.reset');

    Route::middleware(['auth:portal', 'portal.active'])->group(function (): void {
        Route::post('/auth/logout', [PortalAuthController::class, 'logout'])->name('auth.logout');
        Route::get('/me',            [PortalAuthController::class, 'me'])->name('me');
        Route::get('/profile',       [PortalProfileController::class, 'show'])->name('profile.show');
        Route::patch('/profile',     [PortalProfileController::class, 'update'])->name('profile.update');
        Route::post('/profile/password', [PortalProfileController::class, 'changePassword'])->name('profile.password');
    });
});
```

- Register the alias `portal.active` for the middleware in `backend/bootstrap/app.php` (search for existing `alias(...)` block).

File: `backend/app/Modules/Portal/PortalServiceProvider.php`
- In `boot()`, register three named `RateLimiter::for(...)` limiters:
  - `portal-register` → 5/min per IP.
  - `portal-login` → 5/min per (email + IP).

## Edge Cases & Failure Modes

- **Email already used by a staff user.** Portal registration allowed — two tables, no collision. Enforced by `portal_accounts.email` unique constraint (migration).
- **Email already used by another portal account.** 422 with a generic message; do not confirm existence during registration in the wire body used by the sign-in path (registration itself must fail obviously — this is not the reset path).
- **Registration links to a soft-deleted customer.** Reactivate through `Customer` state transition (`backend/app/Modules/Customers/Domain/CustomerState.php`) rather than creating a new duplicate; guarded by `DuplicateDetector`.
- **Password reset for unknown email.** Return 202, do not reveal. `PortalPasswordResetController::sendResetLink`.
- **Token reuse / expired token.** `Password::broker('portal_accounts')->reset` returns `Password::INVALID_TOKEN` → 422; broker enforces single-use + TTL from `auth.passwords.portal_accounts.expire`.
- **Portal account tries to hit `/api/v1/users`, `/api/v1/departments`, etc.** Those routes are behind `auth:web`; the `portal` guard cannot authenticate them → 401. Add regression tests (see Test Plan §3).
- **Staff user tries to hit `/api/v1/portal/*`.** `auth:portal` rejects the web session → 401.
- **Concurrent registration for the same email.** Rely on DB unique index; catch `QueryException` and translate to Problem 422.
- **Rate-limit exceeded.** Return 429 Problem with `Retry-After`. Confirmed via named limiters in `PortalServiceProvider::boot`.
- **RTL correctness.** `frontend/app/(portal)/portal/layout.tsx` sets `dir` from locale; verify no admin-shell CSS leaks.
- **Copy leak of "ticket".** Add a lint test that scans `frontend/messages/*.json` under the `portal.*` key subtree and asserts absence of "ticket" / "تذكرة".
- **Session bleed.** `Auth::guard('portal')->login` on a browser already holding a staff session must not merge; both cookies live under distinct guards. Covered by GuardIsolationTest additions.
- **Half-applied migration** (task 6): if `preferred_locale`/`disabled_at` add fails on production, the down migration must be safe (drop only the two columns). No data loss because both are new.

## Migration / Rollback

- **Forward:** `php artisan migrate` in `backend/` applies `2026_09_04_000100_add_locale_and_disabled_to_portal_accounts.php` if introduced.
- **Rollback:** `php artisan migrate:rollback --step=1` drops the two new columns only. `portal_accounts` core stays intact from Story 2.1.
- **Partial state safety:** If migration ran but code was not deployed, `preferred_locale` defaults to `'en'`; missing `disabled_at` behaves as active. If code deployed without migration, controllers guard column reads via `PortalAccount::$fillable` and default accessors.
- **Config revert:** No changes to `backend/config/auth.php` beyond what Story 2.1 established. Route additions in `backend/routes/api.php` are additive.
- **OpenAPI drift:** If regeneration fails, revert `backend/openapi.yaml` from git before pushing.

## Verification Steps

1. **Backend builds:** in `backend/`, run:
   - `composer install`
   - `php artisan migrate --force`
   - `php artisan openapi:generate`
   - `php artisan test --testsuite=Feature --filter=Portal`
   - `php artisan test --testsuite=Feature --filter=GuardIsolation`
   - `vendor/bin/phpunit --testsuite=Architecture`
2. **Frontend runs:** in `frontend/`, run:
   - `pnpm install`
   - `pnpm lint`
   - `pnpm test`
   - `pnpm dev` — visit `/portal/sign-in`, `/portal/register`, `/portal/forgot-password`, `/portal/requests`, `/portal/account`. Toggle EN ↔ AR; confirm RTL flips.
3. **Cross-guard smoke:** while signed into `/admin`, open a private window and sign into `/portal`. Both sessions coexist; each surface refuses the other's cookies.
4. **Rate-limit smoke:** hit `POST /api/v1/portal/auth/login` seven times with a bad password; expect 429 with `Retry-After` on the 6th onward.
5. **Regression:** `bash scripts/verify.sh` at repo root.

- [x] `/api/v1/portal/auth/register`, `login`, `password/forgot`, `password/reset` are rate-limited with named limiters registered in `PortalServiceProvider::boot`.
- [x] Portal shell exposes exactly three destinations — **My requests**, **New request**, **Account** — with a slim top bar, no sidebar, mobile-first layout, and RTL parity.
- [x] A portal account cannot reach any staff API (`/api/v1/users`, `/api/v1/departments`, etc.) — regression tests prove it.
- [x] Portal user shape contains no roles/capabilities/department; unit test proves it.
- [x] Staff guard cannot resolve a portal account id (`Auth::guard('web')->loginUsingId(...)` returns `null`).
- [x] Copy in `frontend/messages/*.json` under `portal.*` uses "request" and never "ticket" (EN + AR).
- [x] `backend/openapi.yaml` regenerated; drift tests pass.
- [x] `frontend/__tests__/messages-parity.test.ts`, `no-cross-import.test.ts`, and the a11y portal test all pass.

> **The boundary was verified from a real signed-in customer session**, not only
> in tests. A portal account holding a live cookie:
>
> ```
> /api/v1/users           401      /api/v1/portal/auth/me   200
> /api/v1/customers       401
> /api/v1/tickets         401
> /api/v1/admin/settings  401
> /api/v1/audit-entries   401
> ```
>
> **The linking was verified against a customer this system already knew.**
> Layla emailed support in Story 5.2, which auto-created a customer record.
> Registering on the portal with the same address linked to that record rather
> than creating a second one — `created_via = inbound_email`, one customer row.
> That is the case the linking exists for: a portal showing none of somebody's
> own history reads as the product having lost it.
>
> **Deviations from the plan, all deliberate:**
>
> **`loginUsingId` returns `false`, not `null`.** The criterion names Laravel's
> behaviour imprecisely. The test asserts what actually happens and — more
> usefully — proves the property behind it: a staff user and a portal account
> routinely SHARE an id (both tables auto-increment from 1), and the two guards
> still resolve entirely different people, because they read different
> providers rather than because the numbers differ.
>
> **The portal is gated client-side, not by `middleware.ts`.** The staff gate
> asks the staff API who is signed in; routing the portal through it would
> bounce every customer to the agents' sign-in form. The real boundary is the
> API, which scopes to the account's own customer and refuses an
> unauthenticated caller; the client gate only decides which screen to draw.
>
> **`/portal/requests` and `/portal/account` exist now, thin.** Story 6.2 builds
> the list. They are here so the shell's destinations are real pages rather than
> 404s — the failure that left `/tickets` a dead link in the staff navigation
> for weeks.
